title: Read path: memtable first, then only the SSTables that might hold the key
caption: A bloom filter per SSTable answers 'definitely not here' from memory, so most files are skipped without disk I/O.

steps.text: 1. Look in the memtable: the most recent writes are there.
2. For each SSTable, ask its in-memory bloom filter whether the partition key might be inside.
3. 'No' is certain: skip the file with zero disk reads. A 1% false-positive rate means about 1 wasted read per 100 files.
4. 'Maybe': use the partition index to seek straight to the partition and read the slice of rows.
5. Merge the pieces from memtable and SSTables by cell timestamp; the newest value wins. Fewer SSTables (good compaction) means faster reads.
